questions.q: Which of the three tools is the oldest, running on-premises and tied to a SQL Server license?
options: SSIS
Azure Data Factory
Fabric Data Factory
They were all released at the same time
questions.explain: SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS) predates both cloud tools and remains a mature, granular option for on-premises SQL Server shops.

questions.q: What cloud service model is Azure Data Factory, compared to Fabric Data Factory?
options: ADF is PaaS (you configure and manage it); Fabric is SaaS (fully managed for you)
ADF is SaaS; Fabric is PaaS
Both are identical PaaS services
Neither is a cloud service — both run only on-premises
questions.explain: ADF is a platform-as-a-service you configure in the Azure portal. Fabric Data Factory is software-as-a-service, built directly into a Fabric workspace with the infrastructure fully handled for you.

questions.q: In Fabric Data Factory, what replaces the combination of a Dataset and a Linked Service?
options: Connections — data properties are defined inline within activities
Nothing — Fabric requires both a Dataset and a Linked Service, same as ADF
Dataflow Gen2
The On-premises Data Gateway
questions.explain: Fabric eliminates the separate dataset object entirely. A single Connection links to the data source, and properties are defined inline in the activity itself.

questions.q: What is a genuine current gap in Fabric Data Factory compared to Azure Data Factory?
options: No support yet for running SSIS packages
It can't run a Copy activity at all
It has no way to schedule pipelines
It doesn't support any cloud data sources
questions.explain: As of this writing, there's no equivalent to ADF's Azure-SSIS integration runtime in Fabric — organizations with real SSIS package dependencies can't move them to Fabric yet.

questions.q: According to the decision guide in this lesson, what should a company with a stable, working ADF pipeline built over two years generally do?
options: Stay on ADF rather than migrate solely because Fabric is newer
Immediately rebuild everything in Fabric Data Factory
Switch back to SSIS instead
Delete the pipeline and start over in Power BI
questions.explain: Microsoft has kept ADF's feature set stable rather than deprecating it. "Newer" isn't a strong enough reason on its own to migrate a working production pipeline.
